profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, LA2, is located at 900 N. Alameda St., Los Angeles, CA 90012. CoreSite states more than 432,000 square feet on the live facility page, while the operator's own downloadable spec sheet instead gives 424,000 square feet; both are CoreSite's own materials and the discrepancy is noted rather than silently resolved. The building was originally constructed in 1940 as a US Postal Service facility before later conversion to a data center; CoreSite does not state the conversion date. No MW capacity figure is published. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally, though this appears to be portfolio-wide boilerplate rather than a building-specific audit claim.

CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500-plus connected network providers, concentrated in major metro interconnection hubs rather than large single-campus wholesale buildouts, a business model closer to Equinix's than to the hyperscale campus operators tracked elsewhere in this registry.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026. LA2's adaptive reuse of a 1940s postal facility is a common pattern among older urban colocation buildings, which frequently repurpose historic industrial or government structures with the thick floors and loading infrastructure well suited to data center retrofits.

profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite cluster spans Los Angeles, San Jose, Santa Clara, and Santa Clara County, California, the company founding home turf. Wikipedia coverage states CoreSite was established in 2001 as CRG West, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. In May 2007 the company acquired Santa Clara land for a planned 50 megawatt data center as part of a wider expansion that also added Boston and Chicago properties. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. As of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with Los Angeles and San Francisco/San Jose/Santa Clara both listed among its key markets. American Tower completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

CoreSite traces to 2001, when it was founded as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, before rebranding as CoreSite in 2009. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company trading as AMT, SEC filer CIK 1053507, completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought into American Tower's US data center business directly, acquiring roughly 29 percent in July 2022 and increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022.

CoreSite's own site describes a portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets, Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Northern Virginia, Orlando, Raleigh, Silicon Valley, and Washington DC, totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500 or more connected network providers. The company remains headquartered in Denver, Colorado, where American Tower has continued building new CoreSite capacity, including a 180,000-square-foot DE3 facility reported under construction in Denver.

The registry here tracks 19 CoreSite facilities across six states plus Washington DC, California, the District of Columbia, Georgia, Illinois, New Jersey, and Virginia, a subset of CoreSite's 11 named markets. As with Equinix, CoreSite's model concentrates in major metro interconnection hubs rather than large single-campus buildouts, and its ownership structure, a REIT-like data center subsidiary carved out under a publicly traded tower company with a private-capital minority partner in Stonepeak, is a distinct financing pattern from the wholly private-equity buyouts recorded for QTS, CyrusOne, and Flexential elsewhere in this registry.
